To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NTVPM can be applied to predict the cross-country performance (in this case, tractive performance) of a small, light track system on sandy terrain with reasonable accuracy.
the computer-aid model, the Nepean-Tracked Vehicle Performance Model, is applicable to predicting the mobility performance of small, light-weight vehicles.

the physics-based method NTVPM can be used for predicting the cross-country mobility performance of a lightweight track system on deformable terrain; and the results of this study are useful in the design and evaluation of lightweight tracked vehicles for mobility performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of physics-based computer-aided methods for predicting the mobility performance of tracked vehicles on deformative terrain, and the results of the study described here are a step in this direction.

the development of an understanding of the mobility characteristics of tracked vehicles, and with the application of this understanding to the development of computer-aided tools for the design and evaluation of the mobility performance of tracked vehicles.

the development of a physics-based computer-aided tool for predicting the performance of tracked vehicles in cross-country conditions on deformable terrain, and the application of the tool to the prediction of the performance of a lightweight tracked vehicle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study provide evidence for the view that NTVPM is applicable to predicting the crosscountry performance of a small lightweight track system on deformable terrain.
the physics-based, analytical method NTVPM can be used to predict the performance of a light, small tracked vehicle on deformable soil.
, in the absence of experimental data, the computer-aid model NTVPM provides a reasonable estimate of the performance of the track systems under study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physics-based method, NTVPM, is a useful tool to assist in the design and evaluation of the mobility of tracked vehicles.

the physics-based method NTVPM can be used to predict the performance of tracked vehicles, ranging from large, heavy vehicles, such as tanks, to small, lightweight vehicles such as the one studied in this work.
NTVPM is capable of predicting the performance of small, light-weight vehicles on deformable terrains with a high degree of confidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NTVPM can be used to predict the performance of lightweight vehicles on sandy soil.

the NTVPM can be used as an engineering tool for evaluating the cross-country performance and mobility of small, lightweight track vehicles on sandy terrain, as long as appropriate terrain data are provided.

physics-based, computer-based methods, such a NTVPM, are capable of providing reasonably accurate predictions of vehicle performance, provided that the vehicle geometry, track system, and terrain parameters are properly represented in the model.
